newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market hedge funds do well in 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market hedge funds do well in 1st half.

text.p: Hedge funds specializing in emerging market equities posted the best returns for the second quarter and the first half of 1997, continuing a trend begun in 1996, fund monitoring group, TASS Management Ltd said.
Emerging market equity funds monitored by TASS turned in an average return of 11.91 percent for the second quarter and 40.81 pct for the first half, after gains of 36.59 pct in 1996.

"Many emerging market equity funds earned their strong returns from investing in Russia, but in addition some Eastern European and Latin American markets also contributed to the top performance," TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.

European equity hedge funds and global macro funds were the number two and three performers in the hedge funds category for the first half of 1997, with average performances of 16.43 pct and 14.83 pct respectively, TASS said.
For the second quarter U.S. equity hedge funds placed second and European equity hedge funds placed third, with average returns of 7.88 pct and 5.97 pct respectively.

"In sum, performance during the first half was good for most hedge fund categories, although the second quarter was not as solid, but investors seemed to notice the good returns and rewarded funds with more assets in the second quarter," Meaden said.
Assets in the universe of funds tracked by TASS Management grew eight percent to $145 billion from the first to the second quarter.
The main recipients of the new assets were European equity funds, which have seen consistently good returns since last year, TASS said.
"Non-directional/market neutral" funds, which are becoming more attractive to investors nervous about the strength of world financial markets, also received more funds, TASS said.

"Investors are rewarding categories that are performing well, but also are shifting into more conservative strategies as they become increasingly nervous about how much higher world markets can go," Meaden said.
"The flight to non-directional/market neutral funds underscores the fact that investors are trying to diversify their investments to prepare for a downturn," she said.
TASS Management Ltd is a London-based research company which monitors about 1,600 alternative investment managers globally.
The "alternative investment" universe includes hedge funds, CTAs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
